title: Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips
slides: Can Tenstorrent's $6.2B bet on open-weight chips pay off?
The company raised fresh capital at a $6.2B valuation.
Its chips target open-weight AI models, not proprietary ones.
That could cut inference costs for teams avoiding vendor lock-in.
Test one open-weight model on your workload this week.
thread_text:
1. The $6.2B Question

Tenstorrent just raised fresh capital at a $6.2B valuation. Its target isn't the biggest AI labs—it's the teams quietly avoiding vendor lock-in.

2. Open-Weight Only

Its chips are built for open-weight models, not proprietary ones. That means buyers keep control of the model they run.

3. Costs, Not Hype

The real pitch is inference cost. Teams that skip proprietary APIs could cut their per-query spend significantly.

4. The Lock-In Trap

Open-weight chips offer an exit from vendor dependency. But the tradeoff is integrating and maintaining the stack yourself.

5. Test It Yourself

Pick one open-weight model and run a real prompt through it this week. Then compare the output to your current setup.
